problem.title: Per-coordinate fibered Weil-lift extension and jet transport (Direction 4 of the jet-transport scoping round)
problem.user_statement: Notice that jet transport is not a property that must be satisfied by a method for all vector fields in a large enough class. Of course, the class should be as large as possible, as that strengthens the hypothesis and allows for a better classification of methods. I say a large class, because I am not sure if it is possible to state it for all vector fields. This game must be played for all other parts of the puzzle. We don't want this for a trivial Weil algebra, we want it for all that make sense. Or even other extensions which are not Weil lifts if those make sense with jet transport too. The idea, of course, is to understand what jet transport is, and see how that allows us to strengthen the hypothesis. For example, does it make sense to consider extensions wrt to parameters or time or the initial value? Can we use a distinct extension per coordinate of the original system? What about nested extensions? What about nesting extensions on the initial value with extensions in time with extensions in parameters over and over? What about extensions which have Weil algebras of the same dimension? They may be isomorphic, so the method may need to respect some change, that seems to impose extra structure. If all of the above make sense, jet transport is much more that what seems a priori, as it is a combination of all these facts, not only accepting the extension to a Weil algebra.
problem.current_statement: State and test jet transport under a per-coordinate fibered extension, where each coordinate of the original system is Weil-lifted independently rather than the system sharing one global Weil algebra. (Lilith Direction 4, chosen by the user as Round 1's claim.)
problem.intent: Understand precisely what 'jet transport' is as a property so the hypothesis on which methods/vector-field classes/extension types it must hold for can be stated as strongly (generally) as possible. This sub-claim (jt-percoord) tests the per-coordinate/fibered-extension axis specifically, one of 5 directions Lilith produced in the jet-transport Round 0 scoping step (see claim-id 'jet-transport' history in LOG.md / state/rounds/jet-transport-r0.json).
